title: Niemann-Pick disease types A and B
synonyms: Niemann-Pick disease types A and B
summary: Niemann-Pick disease types A and B happen when the body lacks an enzyme that breaks down a fatty substance. It builds up in the liver, spleen, lungs and, in type A, the brain.
inheritance_plain: It is inherited in an autosomal recessive way: a child is affected only if they get a changed copy of the SMPD1 gene from both parents.
carrier_meaning: A carrier has one changed copy. Carriers are healthy and usually do not know they are carriers until they are tested.
disease_meaning: A person with two changed copies has Niemann-Pick disease. Type A starts in infancy and is severe; type B is milder and varies. A treatment now exists for some features and is given by specialist teams. Type C is a different condition with different genes.
screening: A carrier test uses a blood or saliva sample. It looks for the most common changes and cannot find every possible change.
suggested_questions: Someone in my family has Niemann-Pick disease. Could I be a carrier?

card_summary: A fatty substance builds up in the liver, spleen and lungs. Carriers are healthy.
disease_label: Niemann-Pick disease types A and B
carrier_short: One changed copy. Healthy. Can pass the copy on.
disease_short: Two changed copies. Affects the liver, spleen and lungs; severity depends on the type.
care: Specialist metabolic clinics, genetic counselling and family support groups.
